name: In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices Regulation
impact_assessment: joint impact assessment SWD(2012) 273 (executive summary SWD(2012) 274)
evidence_rating: thin: one Commission targeted evaluation (with the Medical Devices Regulation) and industry surveys
summary: The Regulation has applied since May 2022, with long transition periods because most tests now need a notified body. The Commission's 2025 targeted evaluation, covering both device regulations, found safety and transparency benefits but high and often disproportionate costs and reduced availability of some devices; the December 2025 proposal would simplify both.

indicators.objective: No monitoring indicators set in the proposal; assessed through the Commission's reports listed below

literature.citation: European Commission (2025), Targeted evaluation of Regulation (EU) 2017/745 on medical devices and Regulation (EU) 2017/746 on in vitro diagnostic medical devices, SWD(2025) 1051
literature.title: Targeted evaluation of Regulation (EU) 2017/745 on medical devices and Regulation (EU) 2017/746 on in vitro diagnostic medical devices
literature.outcomes: safety; compliance costs; device availability; innovation
literature.headline: Benefits for patients materialising through stronger safety, performance and transparency, but at high and often disproportionate cost; implementation delays, longer and costlier market access, limited notified-body capacity; decrease in availability of some, particularly innovative and niche, devices
literature.summary_plain: The Commission's own evaluation found the stricter rules make devices safer and more transparent, but are costly and slow enough that some devices, especially new and niche ones, have left or not reached the EU market.
literature.quality: Commission self-assessment; data on costs limited

literature.citation: European Commission (2025), Cost-savings accompanying the proposal amending Regulations (EU) 2017/745 and 2017/746, SWD(2025) 1050
literature.title: Cost-savings accompanying the proposal amending Regulations (EU) 2017/745 and 2017/746
literature.headline: Simplification measures in the December 2025 proposal estimated to save around EUR 3.3 billion a year (EUR 0.9 billion adjustment and EUR 2.4 billion administrative costs)
literature.summary_plain: For its proposed simplification, the Commission estimates savings for industry of about EUR 3.3 billion a year.

literature.citation: MedTech Europe (2024), MDR/IVDR survey report (highlights), MedTech Europe
literature.title: MDR/IVDR survey report (highlights)
literature.headline: About half of respondents deprioritise the EU as the first market for new devices; SMEs obtain certificates more slowly
literature.summary_plain: An industry survey reports that many manufacturers now launch new devices outside the EU first.
